question: What is the main focus of Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) in clinical nursing?

options.A: How nurses interact with technology to provide care
options.B: How patients access their personal billing records online
options.C: How software engineers code hospital database networks
options.D: How computer hardware is manufactured in factories

explanation: HCI simply looks at how you and digital tools work together during your daily nursing tasks! [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why is poor software design (HCI) dangerous in a hospital?

options.A: It slows down the hospital internet connection speed
options.B: It increases the cost of buying electrical cables
options.C: It causes computers to overheat and crash frequently
options.D: It can lead to clinical errors and wasted time

explanation: Confusing screens make you waste precious time trying to navigate them, which can distract you from caring for your patients and cause mistakes. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h1)

question: Which software feature measures how quickly a nurse can learn to use a new app?
explanation: Learnability is all about how easy it is for a beginner to pick up a new system and do basic tasks right away. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h2)

question: A nurse accidentally deletes a medication entry, but a pop-up lets her instantly undo it. What design feature is this?
explanation: Error tolerance means the system forgives human slip-ups by making it easy to undo accidental actions. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h2)

question: What type of device is best for scanning medications right at the patient's bedside?
explanation: Portable gadgets let you walk right up to the patient's bedside to verify medications safely and easily. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h3)

question: What is a major design challenge when building screens for smart infusion pumps?

options.A: Operating safely within a compact physical space
options.B: Connecting to high speed wireless gaming routers
options.C: Displaying high definition streaming video content
options.D: Allowing patients to play music during therapy

explanation: Infusion pumps have very small screens, so the buttons and text must be super clear to prevent any dosing mix-ups. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h3)

question: In nursing, what do we mean by 'cognitive load'?

options.A: The mental effort required to process information and complete tasks
options.B: The physical weight of carrying charts around the ward
options.C: The speed at which a computer processor loads a database
options.D: The total number of patients assigned to a single ward

explanation: Cognitive load is simply how hard your brain has to work to think through clinical problems and get your charting done. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h4)

question: How do poorly designed software alerts negatively affect nurses?

options.A: They decrease the physical battery life of bedside tablets
options.B: They increase mental strain and lead to missed warning signs
options.C: They force the operating system to shut down unexpectedly
options.D: They make the computer screen physically too bright to view

explanation: When a system throws too many pointless pop-up alerts at you, it causes 'alert fatigue'—meaning you might start ignoring them and miss a real emergency! [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h4)

question: What is the main goal of a time-motion study when evaluating hospital software?

options.A: To measure how long tasks take and where delays occur
options.B: To test the physical strength of hospital computer monitors
options.C: To calculate the monthly financial cost of software licenses
options.D: To check if the hospital internet cables are fast enough

explanation: Time-motion studies track your steps and tasks to find out where clunky software is slowing you down. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h5)

question: Why do researchers use questionnaires along with observation when testing new software?

options.A: They automatically fix software bugs found in the source code
options.B: They replace the need for nurses to test the software in person
options.C: They measure the exact electrical power consumption of devices
options.D: They capture the user's personal experience and felt difficulty

explanation: Questionnaires let nurses share how comfortable and satisfied they actually felt using the system. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h5)

question: Which software feature helps stop you from accidentally deleting important clinical notes?

options.A: A smaller font size for all medical history text
options.B: A high-speed internet connection in the nursing station
options.C: An automatic password reset every single morning
options.D: A confirmation prompt before completing the action

explanation: A simple 'Are you sure?' pop-up gives you a second to pause before you do something you can't undo. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h6)

question: What is a major clinical risk of using the copy-paste function in electronic health records?

options.A: Corrupting the hospital mainframe database with viruses
options.B: Carrying over outdated or incorrect patient information
options.C: Increased electricity bills for the hospital computer lab
options.D: Slowed down typing speeds for routine nursing notes

explanation: Copying and pasting old notes without double-checking can spread false or old patient data into today's chart. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h6)

question: Why should frontline nurses be involved when designing healthcare software?

options.A: They manage the hospital financial budget and purchases
options.B: They install physical network cables in patient rooms
options.C: They understand actual daily clinical workflows best
options.D: They are trained software engineers and programmers

explanation: Nobody knows how patient care actually flows on the ward better than the nurses doing the work every day! [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h7)

question: What usually happens when hospital management buys software without asking nurses first?

options.A: Workarounds and user frustration that compromise efficiency
options.B: Immediate compliance and flawless electronic documentation
options.C: Lower hospital operational and software maintenance costs
options.D: Instant reduction in patient length of hospital stay

explanation: If a tool doesn't fit real ward life, frustrated nurses will invent risky workarounds just to get their tasks done. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h7)

question: What is a huge benefit of voice-recognition software for clinical documentation?

options.B: Eliminates the requirement for nurse licensure exams
options.C: Allows hands-free dictation of patient notes
options.D: Replaces the need for physical patient beds

explanation: Voice dictation lets you speak your notes quickly while keeping your hands totally free to care for the patient. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h8)

question: How do wearable vital sign sensors improve patient monitoring?

options.A: They prevent patients from ever getting hospital infections
options.B: They completely remove the need for human nursing judgment
options.C: They stream continuous data directly into the electronic record
options.D: They replace all intravenous medication infusion pumps

explanation: Wearables automatically track routine vitals and send them straight to the chart, helping you spot patient deterioration early. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h8)
